title: What you can show in TAK clients
breadcrumb: What you can show in TAK clients

headings.text: GRG rasters — one GroundOverlay per KMZ
Distribution — Mission Packages, missions, Enterprise Sync

blocks.html:
⚠️ Closed alpha — provisional docs. The opendefense-platform is under breaking development; verify against the code before relying on details.

Core ATAK renders only a handful of data shapes natively, and each shape has exactly one mechanism that carries it well — pick the wrong vehicle and ATAK will mosaic your rasters, silently drop your placemarks, or ask the operator to hand-place a PNG on the map. This page is the shape → mechanism → delivery map, so you choose the vehicle before writing code. Everything here was verified on an ATAK-CIV 5.7 client enrolled against the platform's TAK stack (see TAK stack (Kubernetes)); the working example behind it is the Worked example: drone weather in ATAK sibling page, with full source at scripts/dronewx.

blocks.html:
Data shape Native vehicle Arrives on the client via
Live, moving, expiring objects — units, tracks, detections, alerts CoT event TLS stream on port 8089 (or a runtime input on 8090–8094)
Tappable vectors — polygons, lines, points with a details view KML/KMZ, vectors only Mission Package → mission / Available Packages; lands in atak/overlays/
Georeferenced raster — heatmap, scanned map, imagery chip GRG KMZ — exactly one GroundOverlay Mission Package; lands in atak/grg/
Basemap tile pyramid (XYZ/WMTS) custom map source XML Enrollment zip + Default-ATAK device profile
Settings and files every device must have Device profile package Pushed automatically on connect
Self-refreshing overlay from your own HTTP server Network KML link Import Tool → [KML Link], per device, with a refresh interval

CoT events — anything alive

Cursor-on-Target over the port-8089 TLS input is the live SA feed: every marker on the map is a CoT event, and each event carries time/start/stale timestamps — when stale passes, the client fades and drops the marker on its own. That expiry semantic is what makes CoT the vehicle for anything moving or perishable (we verified Digitraffic train and AIS vessel feeds this way); it is the wrong vehicle for a 576-polygon overlay. Any enrolled client certificate can open the 8089 stream — see Pushing data to TAK server. Extra inputs can be created at runtime with POST /Marti/api/inputs on the spare ports 8090–8094, but they are not persisted to CoreConfig.xml — gone on pod restart, so re-POST each run and treat the 500 "Input name already exists" as success.

KML/KMZ vectors — tappable overlays

Polygons, LineStrings and Points in a KMZ render as an Overlay Manager layer: tap a polygon and its description opens in Details (several within tap radius → a deconfliction list). Two hard rules, both learned the painful way: descriptions are plain text plus **<br/>** only (all other HTML is stripped — a <table> collapses to a run-on string), and omit **IconStyle**/**LabelStyle** entirely or every polygon grows a white centre dot. Where layers overlap, the topmost fill wins the tap — hide the layer above to reach the one below. The full authoring detail lives in the sibling page What you can show in TAK clients.

GRG rasters — one GroundOverlay per KMZ

A GroundOverlay (PNG + LatLonBox) imports as a GRG — a georeferenced graphic, individually toggleable per file. The trap: a KMZ mixing several GroundOverlays with Placemarks still imports as one GRG — the rasters get mosaicked into a single image and every placemark is silently dropped. Ship one GroundOverlay per KMZ, and keep vectors in their own KMZ. This is why the demonstrator emits cells.kmz plus separate gust_h00/03/06/12.kmz instead of one combined file.

Basemaps — custom map source XML

Base imagery is not an overlay at all: it is an ATAK <customMapSource> XML naming an XYZ/WMTS tile URL. This is how the Finnish MML maps ship on the platform today — MML_Peruskartta.xml / MML_Ortoilmakuva.xml (Maanmittauslaitos raster via the kapsi.fi community mirror, zoom 2–19) ride inside every enrollment zip and in the Default-ATAK device profile's Maps package, so every client gets them without operator action. How to add your own is the sibling page Defining standard data sources.

Distribution — Mission Packages, missions, Enterprise Sync

Files reach clients wrapped in a Mission Package: a zip with MANIFEST/manifest.xml (MissionPackageManifest version 2, a stable uid, onReceiveImport=true so ATAK imports on download). Never upload a raw KMZ as a package — ATAK unzips it file-by-file and asks the operator to place each PNG by hand ("Select a location on the map to place: h00.png"). Publishing is three idempotent Marti calls (the whole of upload.sh):

PUT  /Marti/api/missions/dronewx?creatorUid=...&defaultRole=MISSION_SUBSCRIBER
POST /Marti/sync/missionupload?hash=<sha256>&filename=...&creatorUid=...   # multipart, field 'assetfile'
PUT  /Marti/api/missions/dronewx/contents                                  # {"hashes":["<sha256>"]}

Every missionupload is listed for all users in ATAK's Data Packages → Available Packages (GET /Marti/sync/search, Tool: public) even without a mission subscription; subscribers additionally get mission change notifications. Endpoint detail: The Marti API (the spec).

Device profiles — push-on-connect

A connection device profile (apply_on_connect=true) pushes packages the moment a client first connects — the platform's Default-ATAK profile delivers default settings, the toolbar, and the Maps package this way; the enrollment zip enables it with deviceProfileEnableOnConnect=true. Right vehicle for configuration and must-have files, wrong one for changing data: profile uploads dedupe by file name, so changed content under the same name is never re-pushed. How a client gets the zip in the first place — programmatically or via the RASENMAEHER UI — is the sibling page Importing a data source programmatically, plus Enrolling & getting a client certificate.

Mentions: video, WFS, network KML

TAK Server can also register video streams and serve WFS feature layers to clients — neither has been exercised on this platform yet, so verify before depending on them. The Import Tool's [KML Link] accepts a network KML URL with a refresh interval, and [HTTP URL] fetches other files (Remote Resources in Overlay Manager) — the only native client-pull mechanisms, configured per device by hand. Note the enrollment templates also cover iTAK, WinTAK and TAK Tracker, but the rendering behaviours above were verified on ATAK-CIV 5.7 only.

What core ATAK cannot do

  • No time slider, no animation. Confirmed against the full feature list — KML TimeSpan changes nothing. Native workaround: one raster per planning step, individually toggleable, plus the per-cell hourly table behind a tap.
  • No rich HTML in details. Descriptions are plain text + <br/>; design your data readouts accordingly.
  • No live HTTP polling from the client. The closest native thing is the per-device [KML Link] refresh. Anything smarter — client-side fetch loops, custom renderers, real timelines — is plugin territory: How ATAK plugins work. The server-push pattern (re-publish a Mission Package on a timer) covers most refresh needs without one.
